This typically happens when a macro defining a global or static variable is not properly terminated with a semicolon.

Upon inspecting the `ZTEST_SUITE` macro definition in `subsys/testsuite/ztest/include/zephyr/ztest_test.h` (lines 199-210), it is clear that the `static const STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(...)` declaration it expands to is missing a terminating semicolon. Other similar macros in Zephyr, such as `K_THREAD_DEFINE` and `Z_TEST`, correctly include the semicolon within their definitions.

The absence of this semicolon causes the compiler to treat the subsequent `void ztest_run_all(...)` declaration as a continuation of the `ZTEST_SUITE` macro's variable definition, leading to the "initializer element is not constant" error. The "expected declaration or statement at end of input" error (line 235 in the error log) is likely a secondary or related parsing error due to the malformed declaration.

The fix is to add the missing semicolon to the end of the `ZTEST_SUITE` macro definition.
